cohort: The study included case files of patients who gave birth in the Buea Regional Hospital (2009-2012) and a comparison of 148 singleton adolescent births with 360 adult births in three health facilities in the Buea Health District (March 1 to August 31, 2013).
finding: The prevalence of teenage births was 13.3%; adolescent pregnancies are more likely to lead to adverse fetal outcomes (low birth weight, preterm babies, low Apgar score) and adverse maternal outcomes (perineal tear) compared to adult pregnancies.
mod_finding: Teenage pregnancies were not significantly associated with an increased risk of caesarean section.
